question: The difference in simple interest and compound interest on a certain sum of money in 2 years at 3% per annum is 90 paisa. What is the sum?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For 2 years, Difference between CI and SI = P × (R/100)²

Difference = 90 paisa = Rs. 0.90

0.90 = P × (3/100)²

0.90 = P × (9 / 10000)

P = (0.90 × 10000) ÷ 9 = 1000

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 1000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given:

Rate (R) = 3% per annum

Time (T) = 2 years

Difference (CI − SI) = 90 paisa = Rs. 0.90

Formula Used: Difference for 2 years (D) = P(R/100)²

 
 Principal (P)
 
• 
 
• 
 Year 1 (3%)
 
• 
 Year 2 (3%)
 
 Difference (CI-SI) = Rs. 0.90
 

 Interest on Interest part

Calculations:

⇒ 0.90 = P × (3 ÷ 100)²

⇒ 0.90 = P × (9 ÷ 10000)

⇒ P = (0.90 × 10000) ÷ 9

⇒ P = 9000 ÷ 9

⇒ P = 1000

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 1000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Difference for 3 Years

The difference between CI and SI for 3 years is given by D = P(R/100)² × (3 + R/100).

Simple Interest Formula

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100, where P is Principal, R is Rate, and T is Time.

Compound Interest Formula

Amount (A) = P(1 + R/100)T and CI = A − P.</p
